about: The sheet for the Main Street Station cutaway: tools/cutaway/sheet.py. Callouts are anchored to drawn parts (history ids, in the isometric view and the flat section); a badge's style is the anchored part's confidence unless `confidence` says otherwise. Callout text is a working draft, written with Claude, for the artist to edit.
title: Main Street Station, 1952
subtitle: Cut through the waiting rooms, from Main Street up to the trains
sectionCaption: The same cut, seen flat: Main Street on the left, the trains on the right

callouts.title: Main Street
callouts.text: East Main Street, in Shockoe Valley.

callouts.title: The loggia
callouts.text: Five stone arches over the front steps.

callouts.title: The main stair
callouts.text: Twelve feet wide and marble, with a landing halfway.

callouts.title: Lower waiting room
callouts.text: Three ticket windows in 1901; by 1969 tickets were sold upstairs.

callouts.title: The waiting room
callouts.text: Marble columns, a coffered ceiling, three double benches.

callouts.title: Restaurant
callouts.text: A lunch counter and tables behind a glass screen.

callouts.title: The concourse
callouts.text: Open to the shed, with a news stand in the arcade.

callouts.title: The gates
callouts.text: Iron rings, and a numbered gate to each platform.

callouts.title: Platforms and tracks
callouts.text: Six stub tracks, five platforms; a through track under each eave.

callouts.title: A C&O Hudson
callouts.text: A 4-6-4 and blue cars, as photographed here in 1953.

callouts.title: A Seaboard diesel
callouts.text: Drawn plain. Seaboard E8s are recorded here in 1955.

callouts.title: The train shed
callouts.text: Riveted steel by Wilson Brothers, 1900, 123 by 517 ft: trusses 18 ft apart, a monitor on the ridge.

callouts.title: On trestles
callouts.text: Steel trestles, and bridges over Main Street.

callouts.title: Baggage room
callouts.text: Under the concourse, with lifts to the platforms; the mail room by 1969.

callouts.title: Offices
callouts.text: Railroad offices; the Railroad YMCA’s rooms in 1901.

callouts.title: The clock tower
callouts.text: 110 ft high, with a clock on each side.

sources: Sources: The Railroad Gazette, July 13, 1900; The Times, Richmond, November 24, 1901; Sanborn atlases, 1905 and 1952; HAER VA-4 and HABS VA-848 (Library of Congress); National Register and Landmark nominations; photographs, about 1905–1971; Official Guide, December 1952; OpenStreetMap; USGS 3DEP.
notes: Rooms are traced from plans published in 1900; their uses in 1952 are not all recorded. Lifted away: the Pullman office, barber shop, ladies’ retiring room and the concourse’s ticket office. From 1920 Virginia’s Corporation Commission could require separate waiting rooms by race; no source found says where they were here.
